constraint: Ten whole unstudied lessons; deadline-driven exam preparation, accepting residual coverage gaps

sequence.title: Subspaces of N-Dimensional Space
sequence.reason: Core zero/addition/scalar-closure criteria for guide problems 2 and 3; supports all later spaces.

sequence.title: Subspaces of N-Dimensional Space: Geometric Interpretation
sequence.reason: Bounded and nonlinear counterexamples directly prepare guide problem 3. Keeps this explicit-guide skill ahead of peripheral transformations.

sequence.title: Finding a Basis of a Span
sequence.reason: Basis definition, independence, deleting redundant generators, original pivot columns and basis expansions. Guide problem 4 and WHW5; also addresses limited basis practice and the missed E2 independence question.

sequence.title: The Dimension of a Span
sequence.reason: Basis cardinality, ambient dimension and dimension computations for WHW5 and the named subspace sections.

sequence.title: The Rank of a Matrix
sequence.reason: Connects pivots, column-space dimension and nonzero echelon rows. Especially useful for the E1 pivot/free-variable mistakes.

sequence.title: The Image and Rank of a Linear Transformation
sequence.reason: Direct image-as-column-span bridge for guide problems 2 and 4; includes image membership and rank(T), consolidating the separate Column Space lesson.

sequence.title: The Kernel of a Linear Transformation
sequence.reason: Consolidates kernel/null-space membership, homogeneous solutions, basis examples and nullity; new textbook5.7 coverage using already practiced elimination.

sequence.title: The Rank-Nullity Theorem
sequence.reason: Explicitly covers rectangular matrices: rank plus nullity equals number of COLUMNS. Intro expands a two-parameter null space into two generators; directly targets the E1 equation/variable-count confusion. Prefer this version over the square-map-only transformation version under this budget.

sequence.title: The Invertible Matrix Theorem in Terms of Linear Transformations
sequence.reason: Combines image, kernel, rank, nullity, collisions and invertibility in conceptual questions. Useful for textbook5.3/5.7 and the prior exams’ question style; does not replace the general injectivity proof.

sequence.title: Rotations as Linear Transformations
sequence.reason: One whole lesson for genuinely new geometric formulas from textbook5.4, protecting some breadth beyond the three sample proof questions. Lowest priority of these ten.
